text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Cement manufacturers slash prices in new year gift to Nigerians planning to build homes.
- Arms and ammunition worth millions of naira allegedly imported by opposition NADECO group seized in neighbouring Benin, says state-owned Nigerian Television Authority.
- Chinese firm contracted to rehabilitate Nigerian railways over 30 months pledges to meet deadline, denying Daily Times report that it had failed to deliver locomotives on schedule.
- Packaging sub-sector bounces back on Nigerian stock market with 6.6 million shares of Studio Press traded on Monday.
- Budget 1997 will contain measures to alleviate the condition of the poor, says finance minister Anthony Ani.
- Fire destroys vegetable oil and livestock cake worth more than a billion naira belonging to Afcott Nigeria Limited and stored in its warehouse ready for export.
- Finance minister Anthony Ani says 1997 fiscal budget likely to be broadcast on Friday.
